## Analysis Summary

**Test image key features:**
- Tomato stem split/peeled open longitudinally
- Interior shows white/cream dry fibrous pith tissue
- **2-3 large, irregular BLACK bodies** (sclerotia) visible inside the hollow stem cavity
- Stem exterior is completely brown/tan and dead
- Dead dry leaves around the plant
- Black plastic mulch visible in background

**Reference image comparison:**

| Class | Similarity | Notes |
|-------|-----------|-------|
| **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** | **HIGH** | White mycelium + dark sclerotia on stems; hollow pith with black sclerotia inside is the hallmark |
| Southern_Blight | LOW-MED | Sclerotia are typically external at soil line; references showed field wilting, not internal sclerotia |
| Alternaria_Black_Molds | LOW | External dark cankers on stem surface, not internal sclerotia inside hollow pith |
| All others | VERY LOW | Leaf spots, fruit rots, or vascular symptoms — no split-stem with internal sclerotia |

**Definitive diagnostic feature:** The large, irregular black sclerotia visible inside the white fibrous hollow pith of a completely dead tomato stem is the textbook hallmark of *Sclerotinia sclerotiorum* (White Mold / Timber Rot). This fungus colonizes the pith, produces white cottony mycelium inside the stem cavity, and forms characteristic black sclerotia that persist inside the hollow stem after death.
